subject: Resource contention: dedicated capacity stall — customer update & remediation plan
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Alex Tan <alex.tan@brightlens.ai>, support@brightlens.ai
Cc: naomi_feldman@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2028-07-22T08:12:00Z
Subject: Resource contention: dedicated capacity stall — immediate status

Hi Alex / BrightLens team,

Quick note to acknowledge the dedicated capacity stall you saw this morning (we flagged increased 5xx and latency spikes across your reserved pool between 07:03–07:46 PT). We immediately routed traffic to your designated fallback model variant and opened additional warm nodes in the US-west region to reduce queuing. You should see request success rates climb back toward normal; metrics show error rate down from ~6.4% at peak to ~0.9% as of 08:05 PT.

What we know so far (initial summary):
- Trigger: abrupt burst of long-sequence jobs from several jobs in your ingestion pipeline that caused KV-cache churn and prevented hot-warm reuse across the pool.
- Effect: autoscaler failed to provision fast enough due to an aggressive cooldown configuration combined with inflated average CPU signal from a transient scheduler-control spike.
- Immediate mitigation: traffic reroute to fallback variant + manual warm pool expansion + priority preemption for interactive routes.

I've attached a short incident timeline (incident-timeline.csv) and a small set of diagnostic logs we collected. We are preparing a technical remediation proposal and a draft post-incident report that outlines root cause, short-term fixes, and the schedule for the permanent fix.

Apologies for the disruption — we know this affected critical flows for your payments/checkout integration. We propose the following next steps:
1) Formal post-incident review with BrightLens engineers — 45 minutes; propose Friday 2028-07-23 09:00 PT.
2) Apply a hotfix to autoscaler thresholds and warm-pool sizing by 2028-07-24 (target).
3) Provide account credit equivalent to two days of average dedicated capacity usage while we complete remediation.

Can you confirm the meeting time works or suggest another? We'll include our SRE lead and product manager.

Thanks — we own this and will follow through.

— Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jordan_blake@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0147

Date: 2028-07-22T08:47:00Z
Subject: Re: Resource contention: dedicated capacity stall — immediate status

Thanks Jordan — appreciate the fast response and the rollback routing.

Two quick asks from our side:
- Please confirm the fallback variant did not change output format for our inference calls (we had a few jobs that expect structured JSON).
- We need an assurance on the timeline — our weekly release depends on capacity stability.

Will join the proposed review Friday if time holds. Please include any temporary configuration changes you applied so our engineers can correlate logs.

— Alex
CTO, BrightLens
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-22T10:03:00Z
Subject: Internal: BrightLens incident — diagnostics and next actions

Jordan / Karthik — quick internal note while we prep the customer-facing doc:

What the infra team observed:
- Root cause hypothesis: autoscaler metric aggregation window was dominated by a scheduler-control spike that surfaced as high average utilization; autoscaler cooldown prevented scale-up for ~4 minutes. Concurrently, the long-sequence requests forced repeated KV cache evictions which increased per-request execution time and kernel selection thrash.
- Contributing factors: warm-pool lower-bound was set conservatively (2 nodes) and warm-up amortization for your workload is higher than the profile we had on file.

Short-term actions executed:
- Manual warm-node add (+6 nodes) to the BrightLens pool (US-west), enforced preemptive priority for low-latency routes.
- Temporarily increased autoscaler sensitivity (reduced cooldown, lowered scale threshold) — note this is a stopgap.
- Snapshot of KV cache metrics and request traces saved: diagnostic-logs-brief.txt attached.

Planned next steps (owner / ETA):
- Karthik: push autoscaler hotfix (thresholds + aggregation window) to canary by 2028-07-23 03:00 PT, full rollout 2028-07-24.
- Naomi: coordinate postmortem draft & RBAC-limited diagnostic share with BrightLens by 2028-07-23 17:00 PT.
- Jordan: communicate customer credit + finalize review slot.

We'll also propose adding a workload-specific warm-pool recommendation to Redwood Optimize for BrightLens to prevent repeats.

— Naomi
Director, SRE Operations
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Alex Tan <alex.tan@brightlens.ai>, support@brightlens.ai
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, product-ops@redwood.com
Date: 2028-07-23T09:12:00Z
Subject: Re: Resource contention: dedicated capacity stall — post-incident draft and fixes

Alex — attaching the post-incident draft (postmortem-draft.pdf) and including the action items directly below. This is the version we'll walk through in today's 09:00 PT review.

Summary (TL;DR):
- What happened: a sudden burst of long-sequence batch jobs from BrightLens ingestion caused KV-cache churn. Autoscaler aggregation window misinterpreted a transient scheduler-control spike as sustained load; cooldown prevented scale-up and requests queued. The queuing increased request durations and further aggravated autoscaler signals in a feedback loop.
- Impact: 43 minutes of elevated 5xxs and tail latency for interactive routes; peak error rate ~6.4%; partial degradation of BrightLens checkout jobs during the window.
- Immediate mitigations taken: fallback traffic routing, manual warm-node expansion (+6), temporary autoscaler sensitivity adjustment.
- Permanent remediation plan:
  1) Autoscaler hotfix: change aggregation from 60s rolling mean to 20s p90-sampled window for burst detection; reduce cooldown to 15s for interactive routes. (Owner: Karthik — canary 2028-07-23, full 2028-07-24)
  2) Warm-pool sizing: bump default minimum for BrightLens to 8 nodes and add a workload profile to Redwood Optimize recommendations. (Owner: Naomi — 2028-07-25)
  3) KV-cache heuristics: add eviction guard when sequence length distribution exceeds baseline; this reduces thrash during large-batch jobs. (Owner: Infra Research — 2028-08-01)
  4) Observability: add a dedicated dashboard and alert that triggers when autoscaler signals and KV-cache eviction rates move in opposing directions. (Owner: Product Ops — 2028-07-26)

Compensation: As noted, we'll apply a credit equivalent to two days of your average dedicated capacity spend; our finance team will send the formal credit note within 48 hours.

Next: We will run the hotfix in canary immediately after this review and monitor BrightLens telemetry closely for 48 hours post-rollout. Please see attached draft for full timeline and logs excerpt.

Meeting link: https://meet.redwood.com/rooms/BRL-incident-2028-07-23

Let me know if you'd like a deeper architecture session; happy to involve our infra research team.

— Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: postmortem-draft.pdf
From: Alex Tan <alex.tan@brightlens.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: support@brightlens.ai, engineering@brightlens.ai
Date: 2028-07-23T15:40:00Z
Subject: Re: Resource contention: dedicated capacity stall — post-incident draft and fixes

Jordan / Naomi / Karthik — thanks for the clear write-up and for moving quickly on the hotfix. We reviewed the draft internally and have three items to confirm in the call:
1) Confirm fallback variant compatibility with our JSON schema (no changes to field ordering or required keys).
2) A timeframe for when we can see the warm-pool recommendation available in Redwood Optimize so our infra team can align.
3) We accept the two-day credit offer; please route the credit note and confirmation to billing@brightlens.ai.

We'll join the 09:00 PT review and appreciate Redwood's ownership here.

— Alex
CTO, BrightLens
